prompt:
You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Variance-adaptive expected maximal inequality for VC-type real classes

## Goal

Build a reusable Causalean theorem for a countable real-valued function class
on a probability space whose expected empirical supremum adapts to the class's
L² radius rather than only its envelope.

## Provides

- A countable-class variance-adaptive expected maximal inequality.
- A statement directly usable without a continuum-supremum measurability assumption.
- Optionally, a set/range wrapper compatible with the existing covering API.

## Statement / milestones

Assume:

- every indexed function is measurable;
- the class has a constant envelope `U`;
- every function has `L²(P)` norm at most `σ`, with `0 < σ < U`;
- the class has polynomial `L²(Q)` covering numbers, uniformly over the
  finitely supported probability measures `Q` used by the empirical metric,
  with constants `A ≥ 1` and exponent `v > 0`.

Prove a universal-constant bound of the standard variance-adaptive form

    E sup_f |n⁻¹ ∑ᵢ (f(Xᵢ) - P f)|
      ≤ C [σ * sqrt(v * log(A * U / σ) / n)
             + v * U * log(A * U / σ) / n]

for `n ≥ 1`, allowing harmless equivalent normalizations of the logarithm
such as `log(max e (A * U / σ))`.  The theorem should be stated so a
countable enumeration can be used directly, avoiding any continuum-supremum
measurability assumption.  A set/range wrapper is welcome if it makes the
existing covering API easier to consume.

The proof should combine symmetrization, localization/truncation or peeling,
the empirical `L²` covering bound, and Dudley chaining.  It must retain the
variance-sensitive `σ` leading term; an envelope-only `U / sqrt(n)` estimate
does not discharge the consumer.

## Standard reference

The standard empirical-process variance-adaptive VC-type maximal inequality,
proved by symmetrization, empirical L² entropy, localization or peeling, and
Dudley chaining. Harmless equivalent logarithmic normalizations are allowed.

## Intended reuse

The immediate paper-local adapter is
`CausalSmith.Stat.BddUniformLogPenalty.vcEntropy_chaining_bound` in
`CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_BddUniformLogPenalty_Research/Causal/EmpiricalProcess/EntropyChaining.lean`.
It then feeds `vcExpectedMaximalInequality` and the frozen theorem
`cty_winsorized_score_maximal_bound`. The theorem is otherwise a reusable
concentration primitive for bounded real-valued VC-type classes.

## May assume / must derive

May assume and reuse:

- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering.RealValuedVCSubgraph.Basic`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering.RealValuedVCSubgraph.Algebra`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering.RealValuedVCSubgraph.Parametric`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering.RealValuedVCSubgraph.Empirical`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Covering.DudleyEntropy`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Rademacher.Symmetrization`
- `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.UniformDeviation.LocalizedEnvelopeExpectation`

In particular, inspect and reuse `HasPolynomialL2Cover`,
`real_vcSubgraph_empirical_l2_covering`,
`real_vcSubgraph_empirical_coveringNumber_le`, and
`real_vcSubgraph_dudley_example`.  The last theorem is currently only a
fixed-sample, envelope-scale signed-Rademacher bound, so an additional
variance-localization argument is required.

Must derive the variance-sensitive `σ` leading term and the second-order
`U/n` term; an envelope-only bound is insufficient.

The promoted module must import only Mathlib/Causalean modules, never a
`CausalSmith/*_Research` module.  Deliver a zero-`sorry`, zero-new-axiom build,
reachable from `Causalean.lean`, with docstrings/index/embeddings/docs updated
under the normal study-promotion workflow.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/VarianceAdaptiveVcExpectedMaximal
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.VarianceAdaptiveVcExpectedMaximal.<Name>
- This is build round 1 of at most 10.

## Your task this turn
0. ASSESS CURRENT STATUS FROM GROUND TRUTH. You are a fresh invocation with NO memory of prior turns — your only context is this prompt plus what you read from disk. Read the current files under the Lean dir and check their real state (remaining `sorry`s and any errors) via lean-lsp diagnostics or a targeted build. Trust the files over the prior round report (a report can lag a partial filler edit). The report and your prior plan below tell you the INTENT; the files tell you the TRUTH.
1. Search the existing library FIRST (run `npm run search -- "<concept>"` in CausalSmith/tools; use lean-lsp local/leansearch) to reuse, not reinvent.
1b. FETCH THE PRIMARY SOURCE when possible. If the Requirement names a reference (or you find the canonical one), fetch it to ground the exact statement, hypotheses, and naming/conventions you formalize — via WebFetch/WebSearch or Bash `curl`/`wget`; for an arXiv paper download the LaTeX source and read the `.tex`, not the PDF. Skip only when no source is named or none is reachable; never block on it.
2. UPDATE `plan_markdown` as a STRUCTURED STATUS LEDGER (this IS the memory the next turn inherits — make it concrete, not a vision doc). Use these sections: `## Done` (decls proven/closed), `## Remaining` (the open sorries, by file), `## Blocked` (what's stuck and why), `## Decisions` (design/API choices + what was tried and rejected, so the next turn doesn't repeat dead ends). Keep it CONCISE — bullet points referencing decl/file names, NOT full proof derivations. Per-lemma proof strategy and tactic sketches belong in the Lean file as docstrings/comments (you write those to disk directly), not duplicated into this JSON string.
3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. Include a `/-! -/` module docstring and a docstring on each public declaration (first paragraph = self-contained NL translation).
3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.VarianceAdaptiveVcExpectedMaximal` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. If a needed reusable prerequisite exists only in a paper folder, escalate instead of importing or copying it; main must extract it into this same temporary tree first.
4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.

- Added `Basic.lean`: exact empirical polynomial L²-cover predicate, normalized log/rate, fixed universal constant, countable empirical supremum, and existing-cover adapter statement.
- Added `Rademacher.lean`: genuine variance-sensitive Rademacher chaining theorem statement with proof route documented in-source.

## Remaining
- `Basic.lean`: prove `HasPolynomialL2Cover.hasPolynomialEmpiricalL2Cover`.
- `Rademacher.lean`: prove `varianceAdaptiveRademacherComplexity_le`.
- `ExpectedMaximal.lean`: prove `varianceAdaptiveExpectedMaximal_le` and `HasPolynomialL2Cover.varianceAdaptiveExpectedMaximal_le`.
- After zero-sorry verification, promote into Causalean, add the root import, and regenerate docs/index/embeddings/headline metadata.

## Blocked
- None. The substantive open work is the empirical-radius self-bounding Dudley argument; existing Dudley results stop at envelope scale.

## Decisions
- Use `[Countable ι]` directly, so no continuum-supremum measurability premise is exposed.
- Require covers only for positive-size empirical laws, matching the proof rather than strengthening to all probability measures.
- Use an exact real cardinality bound, not a ceiled bound; ceiling slack would make the theorem false for arbitrarily small real `v`.
- Normalize with `log(max e (A*U/σ))` and use fixed constant `4096`, preventing a class-dependent existential constant.
- Run one filler this round on the hard core only; all files share an import closure, so parallel fillers would violate the repository build-isolation rule.
